- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If model consistently forecasts below 55% of recent 18-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2–6% in early periods (e.g., 1–7 days ahead) — apply a 1–3% upward bias for short-term horizon.  
- When sentiment shows strong divergence (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00 or -1.00), model may misalign with sentiment direction — adjust forecast to match sentiment trend if it persists for 3+ days.
